pairs.question: Adeone pulchra est?
pairs.derivation: Self-question and answer within the epigram. Question is a genuine interrogative (-ne); answer directly replies. Span ends at the full stop before the next question (Quid ergo...).

pairs.question: Quid ergo in illa petitur et placet?
pairs.derivation: Second self-question/answer in the same epigram. Genuine interrogative (Quid) answered by the one-word reply Tussit, which ends the poem.

pairs.question: Vnde potest auidus captae leo parcere praedae?
pairs.answer: Sed tamen esse tuus dicitur: ergo potest.
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question (Vnde potest...?) answered by the poet himself: it is said to be yours, therefore it can. Answer is the closing pentameter; nothing follows.

pairs.question: Quid dignum tanto tibi uentre gulaque precabor?
pairs.derivation: Self-posed question (Quid...precabor?) answered by the curse-wish it introduces; the answer is the final line. Earlier question (quis furor est?) is not cleanly answered, so not extracted.

pairs.question: Quae ratio est igitur?
pairs.answer: Seruos ibi perdidit omnes et pecus et fructus; non amat inde locum.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange between interlocutors. The buyer's question (Quae ratio est igitur?) is answered by the auctioneer's reply. Speech tags dropped; answer kept contiguous through the full stop ending the quoted reply. The trailing authorial couplet (Quis faceret...) is not part of the reply.
